::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
## TL;DR

Monoculture leans on heavy synthetic nitrogen, and the ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) it volatilises becomes downwind $\text{PM}_{2.5}$. Combining Chinese field-trial data with GEOS-Chem, we find that maize-soybean strip intercropping raises total grain yield $1.5–3.2\%$ while cutting synthetic fertiliser $13.5\%$, ammonia emissions by $0.46\text{ Tg N yr}^{-1}$, surface $\text{PM}_{2.5}$ by up to $2.3\ \mu\text{g m}^{-3}$ and premature deaths by about $7{,}100$ a year. After this module you can trace how a change in field geometry becomes a health number.
:::

## Why monoculture costs clean air

Global agriculture applies over $110\text{ million tonnes}$ of synthetic nitrogen fertilizer each year. In East Asia, heavy fertilization has bought high yields at an environmental cost that arrives in three steps:

1. **Low Nitrogen Use Efficiency (NUE)**: More than $50\%$ of applied nitrogen is lost to the environment rather than absorbed by the crop[^1].
2. **Ammonia Volatilization**: Excess soil ammonium volatilizes into atmospheric ammonia gas ($\text{NH}_3$).
3. **Secondary $\text{PM}_{2.5}$ Smog Formation**: In the atmosphere, basic $\text{NH}_3$ rapidly neutralizes nitric acid ($\text{HNO}_3$) and sulfuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) from industrial and vehicular emissions, forming ammonium nitrate ($\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$) and ammonium sulfate ($(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$) aerosols—the dominant inorganic components of wintertime $\text{PM}_{2.5}$ air pollution in East Asia and the US Midwest[^2].

## What strip intercropping does

**Strip intercropping** is an agro-ecological practice where two or more compatible crops (typically a cereal such as **maize** and a legume such as **soybean** or **peanut**) are cultivated in alternating parallel strips in the same field during the same growing season:

The result is a land equivalent ratio of $1.2$–$1.4$, meaning a monoculture would need $20$–$40\%$ more land for the same grain. ### Three mechanisms at the interface

1. **Biological Nitrogen Fixation**: Legumes form symbiotic relationships with root-nodule *Rhizobium* bacteria that fix inert atmospheric $\text{N}_2$ into bioavailable ammonium, drastically cutting synthetic fertilizer requirements[^3].
2. **Niche Differentiation & Complementarity**: Maize has a deep taproot and tall canopy (capturing upper canopy sunlight); soybean has a lateral shallow root system and shade tolerance (utilizing diffuse ground light).
3. **Interspecific Facilitation**: Maize root exudates stimulate organic acid secretion that mobilizes insoluble soil phosphorus, benefiting both crops.

The net biological productivity of intercropping is measured by the **Land Equivalent Ratio (LER)**:

$$\text{LER} = \frac{Y_{\text{maize, inter}}}{Y_{\text{maize, mono}}} + \frac{Y_{\text{soy, inter}}}{Y_{\text{soy, mono}}}$$

An $\text{LER} > 1.0$ (typically $1.2–1.4$ in field trials) indicates that a monoculture would require $20–40\%$ more land area to produce the same total grain yield.

## From field trials to avoided deaths

In our paper in *Environmental Research Letters*[^4], we coupled agronomic field-trial data across China with the 3-D chemical transport model **GEOS-Chem** and epidemiological concentration-response functions to simulate a nationwide switch to maize-soybean intercropping:

```{=html}
<figure markdown="span">

<figcaption><strong>Figure 2 | The health benefit is not an assumption bolted on at the end; it is the arithmetic consequence of a fertiliser cut carried through two physical models.</strong> Field trials fix the agronomic step, dropping synthetic nitrogen from $10.4$ to $9.0\text{ Tg N yr}^{-1}$ while grain output rises. GEOS-Chem then converts that into $0.46\text{ Tg N yr}^{-1}$ less ammonia volatilisation and, through gas-aerosol partitioning with nitric and sulfuric acid, $2.3\ \mu\text{g m}^{-3}$ less surface $\text{PM}_{2.5}$ over the North China Plain. Only then do concentration-response functions turn that exposure change into $7{,}100$ avoided premature deaths a year. The chain is one-directional and each link is a separate assumption, which is where the uncertainty lives.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

### Nationwide numbers

| Metric | Monoculture Baseline | Nationwide Intercropping Adoption | Co-Benefit Shift |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **National Maize Production** | $215.8\text{ Mt}$ | $+5.2\text{ Mt}$ | **$+2.4\%$ grain increase** |
| **National Soybean Production** | $12.9\text{ Mt}$ | $+1.4\text{ Mt}$ | **$+10.8\%$ grain increase** |
| **Synthetic Nitrogen Application** | $10.4\text{ Tg N yr}^{-1}$ | $9.0\text{ Tg N yr}^{-1}$ | **$-13.5\%$ fertilizer cut** |
| **Agricultural $\text{NH}_3$ Emissions** | $3.45\text{ Tg N yr}^{-1}$ | $2.99\text{ Tg N yr}^{-1}$ | **$-0.46\text{ Tg N yr}^{-1}$ reduction** |
| **Surface $\text{PM}_{2.5}$ (North China Plain)** | $68.4\ \mu\text{g m}^{-3}$ | $66.1\ \mu\text{g m}^{-3}$ | **$-2.3\ \mu\text{g m}^{-3}$ cleaner air** |
| **Annual Prevented Premature Deaths** | — | — | **$7,100$ lives saved per year** |

### Explore the adoption rate

The chain is linear in adoption, so the slider scales grain, fertiliser, $\text{NH}_3$ and avoided $\text{PM}_{2.5}$ mortality together:

::: {.sim-card}
#### 🌾 National intercropping scenario calculator

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof adoptPct = Inputs.range([0, 100], {value: 50, step: 5, label: "Nationwide cropland adoption rate (%)"})

// The chain is linear in adoption, so these are the 100 % nationwide totals.
adopt = adoptPct / 100
maxGrain = 6.6    // Mt
maxFert = 1.40    // Tg N
maxNh3 = 460      // kt N
maxHealth = 7100  // deaths

note = adopt === 0
  ? "Baseline intensive monoculture: high synthetic nitrogen dependency and severe downwind PM2.5 air pollution."
  : adopt < 0.3
  ? "Targeted adoption in high-ammonia hotspots (North China Plain & Sichuan Basin) yields immediate health dividends."
  : adopt < 0.7
  ? "Widespread adoption provides massive fertilizer cost savings for smallholder farmers alongside major public health improvements."
  : "Full nationwide adoption transforms China into a global model of sustainable agro-ecological intensification."

card = (label, value, colour) => html`<div class="sim-readout">
  <div class="sim-readout-label">${label}</div>
  <div class="sim-readout-value" style="color:${colour}">${value}</div>
</div>`

html`<div class="sim-readouts">
  ${card("Total grain boost", `+${(maxGrain * adopt).toFixed(1)} Mt`, "#10b981")}
  ${card("Synthetic N cut", `-${(maxFert * adopt).toFixed(2)} Tg N`, "#38bdf8")}
  ${card("NH₃ emissions slashed", `-${Math.round(maxNh3 * adopt)} kt N`, "#f59e0b")}
  ${card("Avoided deaths / year", `~${Math.round(maxHealth * adopt).toLocaleString()} lives`, "#ec4899")}
</div>`

html`<div style="font-size:0.9em;background:rgba(16,185,129,0.1);border-left:4px solid #10b981;padding:10px;border-radius:4px">${note}</div>`
```
:::


### Data and code

- **Atmospheric Model**: Chemical transport simulations were performed using the open-source **GEOS-Chem Chemical Transport Model**[^5].
- **Agronomic Datasets**: Field trial yield and nitrogen response databases are archived in the Environmental Research Letters repository.
- **Analysis Code**: Geospatial mapping and health burden calculation scripts are open source on GitHub: [`kamingfung/intercropping-air-quality`](https://github.com/kamingfung).

## Key takeaways

- Over half of applied nitrogen is lost; the ammonia it volatilises neutralises nitric and sulfuric acid to form ammonium nitrate and sulfate, the dominant inorganic $\text{PM}_{2.5}$ in East Asian winters.
- Strip intercropping works at the crop interface: legume nitrogen fixation, root-niche complementarity and phosphorus facilitation give a land equivalent ratio of $1.2$–$1.4$.
- Nationwide adoption in China would add $5.2\text{ Mt}$ maize and $1.4\text{ Mt}$ soybean while cutting synthetic nitrogen $13.5\%$, $\text{NH}_3$ by $0.46\text{ Tg N yr}^{-1}$, North China Plain $\text{PM}_{2.5}$ by $2.3\ \mu\text{g m}^{-3}$ and premature deaths by about $7{,}100$ a year.
- Farm field design delivers air-quality gains that industrial controls alone cannot, which is why agriculture, environment and health ministries need to plan together (SDG 2, SDG 3 and SDG 12).
- The practice scales to smallholders: it runs on modern mechanised harvesters and needs little capital compared with carbon capture or end-of-pipe scrubbers.
